resolution: The drag itself now proves its own lag (24fd5a404): every paint drag prints ONE [DRAGDRAW] summary on release — total drag ms, mouse moves, cell-set updates, per-move event-gap avg/max, computePaint avg/max, ghost-build avg/max, and the JS render+commit latency behind each update. The event GAP is the key number: when the engine's frame chokes, mouse events arrive late, so gapMax exposes native stalls JS timers can't see — if gap is huge while compute/ghost/render read low, the cost is the native frame (likely the 4844-piece mesh scene itself), which points at the already-approved static-instance renderer as the real fix. Release-to-standing latency also prints ([DRAGDRAW] paint commit -> standing ms=...), which the 43ms visualBoxes line only partially covered. Drag a long wall and paste the [DRAGDRAW] lines.
